newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish central bank sells dlrs for lira - bankers.
newsitem.headline: Turkish central bank sells dlrs for lira - bankers.

text.p: The Turkish central bank began selling dollars for lira to banks in early afternoon trade on Thursday to restrain dollar demand buoyed by high lira liquidity and political concerns, bankers said.

Banks' lira/dollar rates which had fallen to 134,270, rose to 134,110 during the intervention. Lira which stood at 134,170 per dollar on the screen-based interbank market also firmed to 134,120 due to intervention.
The lira had last closed at 132,600 to the dollar on the interbank on April 17 midday when the markets entered a 6-1/2 day holiday.
Bankers said uneasiness caused by mounting worries over the future of Turkey's Islamist-led coalition government and record high currency in circulation boosted dollar demand.
"The main reason behind rising dollar demand is political uncertainty," said one banker.
Bankers said a firm dollar/mark parity in world markets also supported the U.S. currency in the domestic markets.
Turkish currency in circulation which hit an all-time high of 692.3 trillion lira on April 17 eased to 627.1 trillion lira on April 22, the central bank said on Thursday.
The currency in circulation had surged 50 percent and hit five records in a row between April 11 and 17 due to heavy liquidity demand and public sector salary and pension payments before the holiday.
Some bankers expect the currency in circulation to decline gradually as excess liquidity returns to the banking system after the holiday.
